title: OneTomorrow Donates $7,500 to Rainforest 4 Foundation
author: Stephanie
body:
Estimated to be approximately 180 million years old, the Daintree Rainforest is one of the worlds oldest rainforests, and at 1,200 square kilometres (or 296,526 acres), this stunning expanse of forest plays a vital role in the Australian ecosystem. However, like so many natural wonders, the Daintree has suffered significant deforestation over recent decades, and without intervention we risk losing many indigenous Queensland flora, fauna and animals. Fortunately, the Not-for-Profit organisation Rainforest 4 Foundation is committed to conserving the rainforest for future generations and is gradually buying back the rainforests surrounding land to create protected areas with the hope of re-planting native trees and expanding the Daintree.

Last year, OneTomorrow were delighted to help fund the acquisition of additional acres for Rainforest 4, and this month, OneTomorrow made a further donation of $7,500 towards the cost of planting 1,000 trees on the newly acquired land. This particular planting project will focus on restoring the habitat for the native Southern Cassowary, which has been labelled a Threatened species due to past de-forestation. The cost of planting a tree in the Daintree - which includes site preparation, digging holes, securing plants grown from local provenance seeds, and maintaining the planting - is $10 per tree.

OneTomorrow would like to extend a thank you to all who donated so generously to help restore the rainforest ecosystem. We look forward to continuing our partnership with the Rainforest 4 Foundation and protecting the Daintree Rainforest for generations to come.
